concerns.text: Tasks T035 and T036 mandate statistical comparison of 'FIM vs NL-Control AND FIM vs Baseline'. Spec FR-005 and SC-002 explicitly restrict the required statistical significance test to 'FIM vs NL-Control' only. The baseline comparison is an unrequested scope addition that dilutes the specific hypothesis test defined in the spec, violating FR-005's constraint.

Task T020b requires 'format-based leakage verification' on the synthetic dataset. Spec FR-001 and US-1 acceptance criteria only mandate checking for 'zero overlap with GSM8K examples/caches' and 'no answer keys exposed'. The task introduces a novel, undefined verification step not present in the spec's explicit acceptance criteria, risking scope creep and violating the constraint that tasks must not silently relax or expand requirements.

Tasks T030 and T038 require internal 'time constraint checks' and failing if limits are exceeded within the scripts. Spec FR-006 and FR-007 define these as system-level constraints ('System MUST enforce...') intended for the CI/runner environment. Implementing internal watchdogs in the scripts creates redundant/conflicting error handling and violates the constraint that tasks must not alter the architectural scope of system-level requirements.

Task T027 explicitly instructs to 'Generate Baseline Model' as a build artifact. Spec Assumptions and SC-001 treat the baseline as a pre-existing reference point or control condition ('baseline model... will establish a performance floor') without specifying a generation step. Treating the baseline as a build artifact to be created in this run contradicts the spec's assumption of it being a static reference, violating the constraint on scope definition.
